name: GA-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+21 partisan lean strongly favors Democrats
Jasmine Clark outraised and vastly outspent by outside support versus a low-profile Republican
Open seat after Blair's loss in the full-term nomination, but seat remains safely Democratic
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: The baseline's D+24.8 margin rests on a D+21 lean and a favorable environment, and there is no evidence—no polls, no ratings, no competitive spending—suggesting movement away from it. Clark's strong fundraising and outside backing against an underfunded Republican reinforce Safe D.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending on the Republican side could narrow the margin, though a flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Everton Blair (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Georgia's 13th District is a heavily Democratic, majority-Black Atlanta-area seat with a D+21 partisan lean. David Scott's retirement set off a competitive Democratic primary, which Jasmine Clark won after Everton Blair lost the initial nomination for the full term. The seat itself remains safely in Democratic hands regardless of the primary outcome.

Clark enters the general election with a large financial advantage: over $1.6 million raised and more than $4 million in outside support, with no reported outside opposition. Republican Jonathan Chavez has reported little or no fundraising. With no public polls or expert ratings, the forecast leans on fundamentals and prediction markets, both of which point to a comfortable Democratic win of roughly 25 points.
